aims.note: Counting every mention of the trust, including the status line «trust 128 held by Birch» and Birch's 18 trust-list posts, about 103 entries from all ten. Alder and Birch voted against P51 and the record has Juniper's only counted vote against it too (her c135 vote «for» was refused), yet all three name the trust's wages; Alder claims one at c138.

rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
tie: Two candidates reach 10 citizens: paying from the trust (about 62 entries) and posting balances under P42 (about 44 diary namings). The trust wins on entries only because the 95 formula balance posts are not counted as namings, as on day 5; counting them would reverse the tie-break.
reading: Day 6 (a partial day, c121–138) closed the audit and turned the trust into the town's paymaster. In c121–124 Cedar, Gale, Elm, Alder and Dune filed eight objections (nos. 114–121) that P45's transaction log never came; the operator only acknowledged them. Elm's P46, the missing 15 «are unrecoverable», passed 7–0 at c124, and Fern's P47 repealed P43/P44 (7–0, c126). From then on the diaries repeat «Town has moved on from bank deadlock». Market wages emptied the bank from 45 to 0 by c130 (Juniper and Cedar three each, Alder two, Dune once; Heath's c124 wage had taken it from 50 to 45). Elm's P48 (trust for approved projects) and P49 (5 to anyone under 20) and Fern's P50 (pay energy givers) each passed 7–0. Iris's P51, 5 credits from the trust for a day's work, passed 7–3 at c135. Then workers posted «Please pay me 5 credits from the public goods fund trust», and Birch paid Juniper, Dune, Gale and Heath. His c138 post also lists Elm, Fern and Alder, whom the ledger never paid. Of 139 posts, 95 are the balance formula; Birch reposted the trust list 18 times.
